original_card.question: Can a new local cost interface change the deficit-to-recursive-cost ratio beyond current packing?
methods: Propose a changed helper inventory and derive an optimistic exact moment.
Design a small completed instance and independently verify its endpoint and rank bill.
original_card.acceptance_gate: A new physically realizable contract outside the frozen catalogue whose per-call profile, screened with ceiling.ceiling(), beats the selected word's packing ceiling; a lower cap does not establish identical circuitry or order attainable optima, and is insufficient to pass the stronger-budget target under this model. A scoped local result may be retained without a complete supplier. Expanding it into further construction rounds requires the family-level budget and obligation gate in research-family-status.md; an optimistic passing relaxation alone is not acceptance.

first_step.inspect: Read the selected word's per-call local profile, its packing ceiling and the lever table; run levers.py for the ideal budget of the lever you target.
first_step.scope: Positive control and planning budget only; this is not a new construction or full cold replay.

original_card.first_experiment: Before any synthesis, write the candidate per-call local profile (and centre charge / unpaid coordinates if changed) and screen it with ceiling.ceiling(); reject it if even the ideal ceiling does not beat the selected word's by your stated margin.
original_card.bottleneck_link: Packing of the selected word is capped at +0.87% (ceiling model); only a lower local excess spend or a changed coverage law raises the cap.
allowed_variations: Narrow to one changed boundary or helper type with explicit counts.
If the coverage law, template or guard changes, derive an applicable fully charged replacement bound instead of applying the incumbent ceiling outside its scope.
scope_change_triggers: Mixing only providers already inside the pinned catalogue.
Only changing helper terminal subspaces and monotone frames within the fixed scalar word, entrances and cleanup contract already covered by #1995/#2013.

Continuing a partial cost improvement while leaving the same unpriced consumer, restoration or central-readout obligation unresolved; refresh the family expansion decision first. Local product-retiming evidence has a narrow scope and is not a ban on changed graphs or contracts.

actual_scope: After the #4839 strip-all loss, price one physical word that visits the common chart-1 exit of the centre-chain observation instead of stripping every support, retains every centre-to-Y correction and original return, and test its incremental moment.
scope_change_reason: The catalogue card asks for a new local cost interface. The live handoff 19133212 and #4839's first open question ask for one concrete word that changes the strip costs of this terminal. This package prices that word inside the retained chart model and stops because the moment stays negative.
bottleneck_link: A profitable heterogeneous centre consumer would be a new complex-side local profile. This schedule removes the rank-8 Y strips and all but two rank-9 observation transports, and the remaining width-1 hops still exceed the optimistic rank-8 reward, so it does not supply that profile.
stop_rule: Stop if the changed word's optimistic incremental moment is negative throughout C in [0,1], including the relaxation that makes the width-9 round trip free.
evidence: verify.py prints PASS_SHARED_CHART_CENTRE_VISIT_STILL_LOSES and matches RESULT.json. All 37 selections match the strip-all endpoint and the raw inverse transpose. Centre 0 costs 112 width-1 hops plus 2 width-9 transports; the uniform upper bound is -113, and -104 if the width-9 round trip is free.

open_questions.question: Can a producer whose affected Y registers are not 112 private width-8 subspaces of chart 1 avoid the width-1 hops while restoring every demanded output?
open_questions.why_it_matters: The width-9 centre round trip is not the obstruction: the moment stays negative even if those two transports are free.
open_questions.first_step: Name a source-bound exit frame in which at least two affected Y fields already coincide, and price one correction on that shared frame.
open_questions.blocked_by: In the pinned frames the 112 Y charts are pairwise distinct subspaces of chart 1.

open_questions.question: Does a changed output contract delete centre-to-Y corrections instead of transporting them?
open_questions.why_it_matters: Every retained correction currently costs two width-1 hops, and 112 hops already exceed one rank-8 reward.
open_questions.first_step: State which of centre 0's 56 Y outputs may legally remain contaminated, then reprice only the retained corrections.
open_questions.blocked_by: That permission has to come from the caller contract. Omitting a correction inside this terminal changes the endpoint.
